gist: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious after a failed lethal injection execution.
Lawyers claim prison officials botched the execution by failing to insert IV lines correctly.
Tennessee's governor ordered an independent review and halted all executions for the year.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious and on a ventilator following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion to preserve evidence, alleging prison officials botched the lethal injection. They state officials used at least seven needles, bending one, while Pike whimpered and cried. An expert suggested the drug pentobarbital entered tissue under her skin rather than her bloodstream due to ruptured veins or blood clots.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions in the state for the year and ordered an independent review. Pike's lawyers had previously warned that her blood-clotting condition and small veins risked causing unnecessary pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities have not yet said whether they will attempt to execute Pike again, and her lawyers are seeking to preserve all physical, written, and electronic evidence.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: PC makers revealed details for the first laptops powered by Nvidia's RTX Spark chip. Microsoft announced its Surface Laptop Ultra, which TechCrunch notes starts at $2,600 (The Verge reports $2,599 across manufacturers) and climbs to $5,900. Microsoft also unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box workstation starting at $6,000. Dell detailed its Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition at $3,800. A fully configured Asus ProArt P16 costs up to $6,999.99.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The machines are built to compete with high-end MacBook Pros, targeting creators, developers, and local AI users. They feature revamped Windows 11 software with Execution Containers to help sandbox AI agents. To entice developers away from Apple, Microsoft is offering trade-in discounts of up to $1,000 for MacBook Pros.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The new laptops launch in October, arriving as early as 16 October, with Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition pre-orders scheduled for late October delivery.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US government has suspended Microsoft and seven other technology firms, including Adobe, from a program that helps foreign workers obtain permanent US residency. Vice President JD Vance accused the companies of abusing the H-1B visa system to replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. The Department of Labor announced it will not process new or pending applications from these firms.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Vance claimed Microsoft laid off American workers while filing thousands of visa applications, undercutting domestic wages. Microsoft rejected these allegations, stating that eighty per cent of its H-1B filings were for existing employees rather than new hires, and that its international staff receive the same compensation as US workers. Immigration advocacy groups argue that attracting global talent benefits the US economy, while Vance described the visa recipients as "indentured servants".

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Microsoft plans to provide the US administration with additional information regarding its hiring practices. Meanwhile, the US government has proposed eliminating the sixty-day grace period for laid-off visa holders.

gist: Peter Greenaway's assisted dying drama starring Dustin Hoffman is stuck in post-production hell.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Filming began in Lucca, Tuscany, in late 2023 after initial cashflow delays. The production faced further issues when producers made a separate, more commercial cut without the director, citing budget overruns. Two unfinished versions now circulate while rights remain contested.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A masked gang of at least seven people stole 30,000 bottles of prestigious wine, worth €5m, from the Marchesi Antinori winery in Tuscany. sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: This is the largest wine theft of its kind in Italy. The stolen bottles, including prized Tignanello and Solaia reds, are highly valued. Outlets disagree on the price per bottle, reporting ranges of €150 to €500 or €120 to €400. The winery's insurance does not cover the loss.

sections.heading: What happens next

gist: Presenter Alison Hammond feared she was having a heart attack during a live broadcast.
She rushed off air and was hospitalised, but had suffered a panic attack.
Hammond returned to the show a week later to discuss her experience.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: During a live broadcast of ITV's This Morning last Friday, presenter Alison Hammond rushed off air after experiencing what she feared was a heart attack. She was taken to hospital, where tests revealed she had actually suffered a panic attack. Hammond described the experience as "very real" and one of the scariest things she had ever been through.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlighted the intense pressure of presenting live television. Returning to the show a week later, Hammond and psychologist Dr Sian Williams discussed panic attacks to raise awareness. Williams explained that panic attacks represent "anxiety on overdrive" and can feel identical to heart attacks due to shared physical symptoms like chest pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hammond has returned to her regular presenting slot on This Morning. She noted that the health scare has given her a new perspective, prompting her to take stock of her health.

fivew: She suffered a panic attack on air that she mistook for a heart attack.
The incident occurred last Friday, and she returned to the show this Friday.
The event took place live on the ITV programme This Morning.
The sudden rush of adrenaline caused severe shortness of breath and chest tightness.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor surrendered his lease on Royal Lodge, incurring dilapidation and repair charges. Deducting £302,000 in early departure compensation left £1.5m owed to the landlord. The King covered this settlement using private funds, though The Times reported that he contributed to the repair costs.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The King intervened to ensure the Crown Estate was not left out of pocket. Mountbatten-Windsor had previously relocated to Sandringham amid controversy surrounding his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. While his upkeep is funded by the King, his brother will not finance his legal battles over police search warrants.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Royal Lodge will be marketed commercially by two recognised agents to provide returns for the nation, with no plans for another royal resident.

gist: Nikon disqualified a scientific photography contest winner for using generative artificial intelligence.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Nikon disqualified Dr Ning Xu's winning video in its Small World In Motion contest. Scientists flagged that the video, depicting hair-like structures in a child's airway, appeared fabricated. Xu admitted using AI for post-processing but denied generating the actual motion or cells. Nguyen Nam Nhat was named the new winner.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts, including Dr Robert Hirst, warned that the cells did not resemble real samples from patients with the respiratory condition. The controversy has impacted patients, doctors, and scientific networks globally, raising questions about the authenticity of microscopic imagery in prestigious competitions.

sections.heading: What happens next

gist: Spanish archaeologists cataloged 597 wooden remains left by Neanderthals in stone molds.
The finds from Abric Romaní include bark trays, shelters, and a unique wooden club.
The discoveries indicate that woodworking was a routine and complex activity for Neanderthals.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: At Abric Romaní in Spain, mineral-rich water coated wooden Neanderthal tools in limestone crust. As the wood rotted, it left hollow molds. Spanish archaeologists cataloged 597 wooden remains dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago, including thirteen modified tools like spears, bark trays, and a club.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Because wood rots quickly, very little is known about Paleolithic woodwork. These finds show that woodworking was routine for Neanderthals, demonstrating planning and cognitive complexity that challenge the perception of Neanderthals as simple.

sections.text: A Kenyan businessman fell ill in DR Congo, visited several medical facilities, and crossed into Uganda. He then flew to Nairobi via Entebbe, passing airport temperature screenings undetected. Diagnosed with Ebola after arriving at Nairobi Hospital, he died on 5 October.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident exposed weaknesses in regional biosecurity and airport screening during an outbreak that has killed over 4,000 people in DR Congo. Experts warned that relying solely on temperature checks is limited, as medications or absence of fever can mask symptoms.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kenyan authorities have quarantined potential contacts, while tracing continues across DR Congo and Uganda. The WHO is working to counter fear and misinformation, warning that stigma discourages people from reporting symptoms and seeking timely care.

gist: Ava DuVernay has directed 14th, a documentary focusing on the US 14th amendment.
The film features legal experts and politicians examining civil rights and American democracy.
The documentary is premiering at the New York film festival before streaming on Netflix.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Director Ava DuVernay created a 110-minute documentary titled 14th, following her previous film 13th. The documentary focuses on the five-point 14th amendment, utilising archive imagery, music, and interviews with figures such as Sherrilyn Ifill, Bryan Stevenson, Stacey Abrams, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The film argues that the 14th amendment serves as the foundation for multiracial democracy, protecting birthright citizenship, due process, and voting rights, while examining historical backlash from Reconstruction to modern political movements.

sections.text: In September 2022, underwater explosions ruptured the Nord Stream pipelines beneath the Baltic Sea. gist: A new study reveals that psilocybin creates hidden order in brain activity rather than pure chaos.

sections.text: New York City emergency medical services staff are facing low wages, with starting salaries of $39,386. sections.text: Australia leads the world in electricity generated per person from solar panels. sections.text: High electricity prices, government schemes cutting upfront costs, and low-density housing with ample roof space have driven the boom. Rooftop solar now supplies almost fourteen percent of the country's electricity over the past year, downplaying coal. Households with solar and batteries enjoy substantially lower bills, and surplus solar power has caused wholesale electricity prices to drop to zero or go negative during midday.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US justice department launched an investigation into five major television networks—ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News. It requested communications to establish whether their temporary suspension of presidential pool coverage breached federal antitrust laws. The suspension occurred after the Trump administration revoked access for reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico. The outlets successfully challenged the restriction in court, and their credentials were later reinstated.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The justice department warned that the boycott might violate the Sherman Act against monopolistic practices. Pool members typically share broadcast material across the wider media. The investigation forms part of broader administration disputes with press organisations, which included taking direct control of the press pool and barring Associated Press journalists over geographical wording.

gist: Family calls for allergy ratings after a girl died from an unwashed blender.
A cafe and its proprietor were fined following a fatal allergic reaction.
Food safety officials emphasise that businesses must take allergen risks seriously.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A 12-year-old girl died of anaphylactic shock after drinking a milkshake from a south-east London cafe. The blender used had not been washed after making a previous drink containing tree nuts. The cafe and its proprietor were subsequently fined after admitting charges related to food safety.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The family argue that current food hygiene ratings do not inform consumers about a business's allergy management systems. They are campaigning for a dedicated allergy rating scheme so people with food allergies can make safer choices.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Food Standards Agency states it is keeping its policy under review and has produced new guidance and training for businesses regarding allergen responsibilities.

fivew: Mia St Hilaire and her family.
A 12-year-old girl died after drinking a milkshake containing hazelnut residue from an unwashed blender.
Pop Inn Cafe in Bermondsey, south-east London.
Cross-contamination occurred because the cafe blender was not cleaned between orders.

quotes.text: Food businesses must take allergen risks seriously, every time.

sections.text: Michael Bogle was released from HMP Wandsworth on 1 October under the government's early release scheme. Within four days, he stole more than £100 worth of detergent from north London supermarkets. He was arrested on Tuesday, admitted the offences on Wednesday, and received an eight-month sentence for breaching a suspended sentence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: A senior police officer raised concerns that releasing high-risk offenders transfers pressure onto policing and puts communities at risk. The Ministry of Justice defended the scheme, stating it was necessary because the prison system was on the brink of collapse.

fivew: A prisoner released early under a government scheme was jailed again for shoplifting.
To relieve pressure on dangerously full prisons across England and Wales.

quotes.text: Keep the early release going. It's good.
We inherited a prison system on the brink of collapse.

sections.text: England won 3-1 against Greece in Crete on Friday night during their Women's World Cup qualifying play-off first leg. Maya le Tissier scored in the 63rd minute, while Sarina Wiegman handed debuts to Erica Meg Parkinson and Grace Fisk.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory gives England a first-leg lead as they attempt to secure their place in Brazil next year. However, defensive lapses and a failure to keep a clean sheet left Wiegman admitting frustrations over the team's sloppiness.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: England will face Greece again in the second leg on Tuesday in Leicester to finish the job, with the winner advancing to face Ukraine or Slovakia in round two.

gist: Cristiano Ronaldo was provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation.
Ronaldo walked out of the international camp after being left out of the starting line-up.
The FPF president stated there is a desire to have the captain back.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cristiano Ronaldo was provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation after walking out of Portugal's international camp in September. He left following matches against Norway and Denmark. The forward explained that coach Jorge Jesus broke his word, creating an absolute breach of trust. Ronaldo apologised to his team-mates and fans, accepting that he deserved to be punished.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Under FPF rules, players who walk out on international duties face a ban of one to six months and a fine. The case has been marked as urgent.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: A normal disciplinary process will take place. FPF president Pedro Proenc stated that there is a strong desire to have their captain back with the team.

sections.text: Chelsea secured a 5-1 victory against Bournemouth on Saturday. Jordan Henderson scored his first two goals for the club, including an opening effort and a free-kick, and assisted Morgan Rogers. Moises Caicedo played a deep midfield role in his 150th appearance for the club, helping provide balance and defensive stability.

sections.text: Chelsea have scored heavily this campaign with 15 goals from six matches, but conceded 13. The pairing of Henderson and Caicedo brought much-needed control and defensive stability behind the attacking trio of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, though the team is still awaiting their first clean sheet of the league campaign.

gist: Manchester City appeal a guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules.
City face intense hostility from Liverpool supporters at Anfield in their next match.
The Premier League is considering punishments, including potential points deductions, expulsion or relegation.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester City were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18. The independent commission described dealings as a sham, alleging artificially inflated revenue. City maintain their innocence and have launched an appeal against the ruling.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: City visit rivals Liverpool at Anfield facing intense hostility from fans who feel aggrieved over previous title races. The verdict creates uncertainty across the Premier League, with potential punishments including points deductions, relegation, or expulsion shadowing City's current position at the top of the table.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: City face Liverpool on Sunday under an appropriate police plan. The Premier League will weigh up punishments while City's appeal undergoes a lengthy legal process.

sections.text: Northampton defeated Bath 71-48 in a high-scoring game featuring 18 tries. Northampton pulled away in the second half after both sides surpassed 100 points with 15 minutes remaining.

gist: Max Verstappen secured pole position in Singapore, continuing his strong late-season Formula 1 form.
McLaren drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri collided on the final lap of the sprint.
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella described the inter-team collision as unacceptable and serious.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Max Verstappen took pole position in Singapore after winning the earlier sprint race. Meanwhile, McLaren suffered a disastrous end to the sprint when team-mates Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri collided on the final lap while battling for position. The incident resulted in Piastri retiring and Norris dropping to eighth place.

sections.heading: Why it matters

gist: Bruno Guimaraes came off the bench to secure a 2-1 win against Leeds.
Piero Hincapie suffered an injury scare after being carried off during the warm-down.
Arsenal moved level on points with league leaders Manchester City.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Arsenal came from behind to beat Leeds 2-1 at Emirates Stadium. After falling behind in the 55th minute, Riccardo Calafiori equalised before substitute Bruno Guimaraes scored the winner. Defender Piero Hincapie was later carried off with an injury during the warm-down.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory moves Mikel Arteta's side level on points with league leaders Manchester City. However, defensive frailties and attacking struggles continue to raise concerns about their title defence.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Arsenal face an anxious wait to discover the severity of Piero Hincapie's right ankle injury following his departure from the pitch.

timeline.text: Boos, anguish & fading belief -'worrying day' for under-pressure Carrick

gist: Manchester United failed to beat 10-man opponents for the second successive home game.
Manager Michael Carrick faces growing pressure after a late equaliser against Tottenham.
Pundits highlighted physical and tactical shortcomings as fans showed frustration.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester United conceded an injury-time equaliser against a Tottenham side reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur's red card. Dominic Solanke scored past goalkeeper Senne Lammens after Lisandro Martinez was outmuscled, leading to boos from fans at the end of the match.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Manager Michael Carrick is under severe pressure as belief begins to ebb away. Pundits noted that opponents consistently outrun United, and the team is struggling defensively in key moments, failing to secure necessary points.

fivew: Manchester United failed to beat 10-man Tottenham after conceding a late equaliser.
Defensive mistakes and a physical disadvantage led to dropped points and mounting pressure.

quotes.text: A worrying day for Michael Carrick
The stats don't lie when every time the other team runs more than you
